reading.text: At a neighborhood bicycle shop, a customer brings back a helmet with a broken strap two days after purchase. The service assistant checks the receipt and inspects the item before offering options. Store policy allows a refund to the original payment method when an item is faulty; a different color can be exchanged if stock is available. The assistant explains that a repair would take three days, then asks which solution the customer prefers. After agreeing on a refund, she enters the reason in the service log and gives the customer a copy. At the end of each month, the supervisor reviews similar cases to find repeated product faults. If several helmets show the same problem, the shop contacts the supplier and pauses new sales until the issue is checked.
